title: Surge mitigation: working-set surgery, reservation rebalance, and adaptive burst ladder
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a mixed-tenant surge on 2026-03-08 we observed sustained high eviction rates in 3 dedicated clusters. Root cause analysis shows a combination of a single tenant expanding a large working-set (memory & KV usage), aggressive soft-bursting on several reservations, and a reservation sizing heuristic that overallocated headroom for inactive tenants. Impact: degraded tail latency for P99 inference requests, elevated container restarts, and two partial SLA breaches for affected customers. Goal: implement a low-risk, staged remediation that isolates loud working sets, recalibrates reservation accounting, and replaces the current single-threshold burst with an adaptive ladder that prevents runaway burst consumption while preserving short, legitimate spikes.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Noisy tenant detection rule in prod that triggers soft-fence within 5m of sustained working-set growth (memory or KV) and reduces available burst by >=50% for offending tenant.
2) Reservation rebalance job that recomputes baseline reservations weekly and reapplies with safe rollouts (canary 1%, 10%, 100%) without evictions.
3) Adaptive burst ladder deployed behind a feature flag controlling max burst step-down per minute; experiments show tail latency improvement and no regression for median latency on synthetic tenant tests.
4) Runbook updated with exact mitigation steps, telemetries and dashboard links.
comments: 2026-03-10 — Aisha Patel: Initial incident writeup and hypothesis posted. Key signals: KV cache footprint per-tenant doubled in 30 minutes; burst tokens depleted for tenant T-311; control-plane decided to throttle tenant after the second SLA alert. Attaching heap profiles and KV heatmaps.

2026-03-11 — Marco Rivera: Added triage notes after deeper forensics. Hypothesis refined: not a single bad workload loop but an opportunistic set of model warmups that expanded per-tenant working set across multiple nodes causing cross-tenant cache pressure. Suggested mitigations: (1) 'working-set surgery' probe to snapshot per-tenant memory/kv and evict lightly used prefixes, (2) reservation rebalance recalculation that avoids round-up heuristics for inactive tenants, (3) adaptive burst ladder throttler modeled as multi-step decay rather than single-shot hard cap.

Breaking work into three parallel streams: detection rules + fencing (owner: Marco), reservation rebalance job and safe rollout (owner: Priya Shah), adaptive burst ladder service and feature flag (owner: Daniel Kim). Each stream has test jobs and synthetic tenants for validation.
